title: Deep learning on health records builds a one-year suicide attempt early-warning model
summary: Machine-learning algorithms and deep neural networks were trained on electronic health records to produce a calibrated risk score for suicide attempt in the following year. The model reached AUC 0.792 in the retrospective cohort and 0.769 in prospective cohorts, and the very-high-risk category had a suicide attempt rate 60 times the population baseline in the prospective cohorts. Mental health disorders, substance abuse, utilization indicators and socioeconomic determinants were associated features; the risk score is a stratification tool, not a causal result.
